# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 ESC (Job #5): Design Model

## 0. Scope and Assumptions

No MOSFET, gate driver, board stack-up or ESC firmware was specified, so I fixed a reference design. Every result below is shown symbolically first, so you can substitute datasheet values once parts are chosen. Items marked **[VERIFY]** must be checked against the actual datasheet or the ArduPilot source before tape-out.

**Architecture clarification.** The STM32H743 is the flight controller MCU. It runs ArduPilot and generates DShot. The 48 kHz complementary PWM is generated by four separate ESC MCUs, which commutate the motors. The reference uses one AT32F421 running AM32 per motor. The H743 never drives the FETs directly.

| Parameter | Symbol | Reference value |
|---|---|---|
| Battery (6S, full) | V_bus | 25.2 V |
| Burst phase current | I | 80 A (per motor) |
| PWM frequency | f_sw | 48 kHz |
| Burst duty | D | 0.90 |
| MOSFET (40 V, PDFN 3.3×3.3 class) | R_ds,25 | 1.5 mΩ max @ V_GS = 10 V |
| R_ds temperature coefficient | α | 0.006 /K **[VERIFY]** |
| Gate charge | Q_g / Q_gs2 / Q_gd | 30 / 4 / 6 nC |
| Miller plateau | V_pl | 3.5 V |
| Output charge | Q_oss | 20 nC |
| Reverse recovery (80 A, hot) | Q_rr | 60 nC |
| Body diode V_f | V_f | 0.8 V |
| Gate driver (FD6288-class) | R_src / R_snk | ≈ 5 Ω / ≈ 2.5 Ω |
| External gate resistor | R_g | 3.3 Ω (plus ~1 Ω internal) |
| Gate drive supply | V_drv | 10 V (dedicated LDO/buck) |
| Dead time | t_dt | 60 ns per edge |
| Junction-to-case thermal resistance | R_θJC | 1.2 K/W |

## 1. Conduction Loss Model

### 1.1 Conduction topology (6-step trapezoidal, complementary PWM, as in AM32)

In each 60° commutation sector, two legs are active:

- The **PWM leg**: the high side (HS) is on for fraction D, and the low side (LS) synchronously rectifies for (1 − D).
- The **return leg**: its LS is fully on.

Over one electrical revolution, each leg spends 120° as the PWM leg, 120° as the return leg, and 120° floating. This gives the per-FET RMS factors:

$$
P_{HS}=\frac{D}{3}I^2R_{ds}(T_j),\qquad
P_{LS}=\frac{(1-D)+1}{3}I^2R_{ds}(T_j)=\frac{2-D}{3}I^2R_{ds}(T_j)
$$

Summing over the three legs gives the per-motor total:

$$
P_{cond,motor}=3\left(\frac{D}{3}+\frac{2-D}{3}\right)I^2R_{ds}=2I^2R_{ds}(T_j)
$$

This is a sanity check: two switches are always in the current path. The LS is the hottest device for any D < 1.

### 1.2 Temperature-dependent R_ds(on)

$$
R_{ds}(T_j)=R_{ds,25}\,[1+\alpha(T_j-25)]
$$

Solved self-consistently with the thermal model in §3, this converges at about T_j ≈ 100 °C:

R_ds(100 °C) = 1.5 × 1.45 = **2.18 mΩ**, so I²R = 6400 × 0.00218 = **13.95 W**.

| Quantity | Formula | Value |
|---|---|---|
| HS FET | 0.9/3 × 13.95 | **4.19 W** |
| LS FET (worst device) | 1.1/3 × 13.95 | **5.12 W** |
| Per motor | 2I²R | **27.9 W** |
| 4-in-1, all motors at 80 A | ×4 | **111.6 W** |
